The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
President Trump made a campaign stop in Kentucky yesterday,
where he threw his support behind Republicans facing tight midterm races.
Zach Carion reports from member station WVXU in Cincinnati.
Trump says if Republicans lose, Democrats will undo his administration's work from its
first two years back in office.
That's why he says these midterms are important in solid red Kentucky and in nearby Ohio,
where Democrats could make gains.
If they win the midterms, all of a sudden you're going to see a slide.
And all of the crap that we talk about, the incompetent stuff that we talk about,
is going to come back and we're going to go through the same process.
And I don't think our country can handle it again.
Kentucky Republicans are expected to win their races, but in Ohio,
GOP candidates are in tougher battles like incumbent Senator John Husted,
who's facing former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown.
For NPR News, I'm Zach Carion in Highland Heights, Kentucky.
A man and a six-year-old boy were killed yesterday and 11 others injured
when a truck drove through a crowd of people at a youth sports complex in Wichita, Kansas.
Roger Noemmer has the story from member station KMUW.
Police say they are still trying to piece together why a woman with two kids in her
truck allegedly drove through a field where children were playing soccer.
Wichita City Councilmember Becky Tuttle says she feels for the families and onlookers.
My heart breaks not only for the people that were personally impacted,
but anybody who maybe observed the horrible tragedy that happened today.
Wichita Police Captain Aaron Moses says the driver of the truck is in custody
and cooperating with authorities.
We have a really good idea of what happened.
What we're working to do now is do the investigation to determine how it happened and why.
Officials are asking anyone with video or photos from the incident to share them with police.
For NPR News, I'm Roger Noemmer in Wichita.
The shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon last week has rattled the community
and the country. Oregon Governor Tina Kotak says she's grateful for the condolences.
I really appreciate all the outpouring nationally of just well-wishes and condolences coming from
across the country and people just wanting to know how they can help.
And we're still in that first 48 hours of just trying to understand it.
And it's going to be a couple more days before we know all the details.
The shooting killed three children in their classroom along with a teacher.
The suspect was a 16-year-old and former student at the school,
a parent who has children who attend that school shot and killed the teenager.
Canada's Defence Minister says several people have been killed and injured in an incident
at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire.
Fire crews have been working to contain the flames that are being fanned by fierce winds.
You're listening to NPR.
A dangerous Category 4 typhoon passed 10 miles south of Guam yesterday.
It toppled trees and knocked out power, but the island managed to escape major damage.
Dana Williams of member station KPRG reports from Guam.
Emergency managers feared typhoon Champi would cause extensive damage in this U.S. territory,
but the storm's compact wind field and relatively fast passage
prevented what could have been a major disaster.
Brandon Eyelid of the National Weather Service says while the storm's
eyewall packed winds of 140 miles per hour,
gusts at the Guam airport just 20 miles away barely exceeded 80 miles per hour.
He says shortly after the storm made its closest point of approach,
Champi was upgraded to a super typhoon with winds of 150 miles per hour.
I don't know if you can split it closer than that,
having a super typhoon this close and not have impacts even 20 miles to the north.
Champi is the third super typhoon recorded in the Mariana Islands so far this year.
For NPR News, I'm Dana Williams on Guam.
Japan is getting ready to launch a spacecraft Tuesday on the world's first mission to Phobos,
one of the two small moons orbiting Mars.
Scientists hope the mission will provide insight into the origins of life in the solar system.
Samples from the mission also are expected to provide important data
as scientists consider the possibility of building a Martian moon base for a future manned mission.
Japan is leading this mission, but it is using equipment and communication support from NASA.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News.
